quotes.text: By meeting maximal courage with righteous, bountiful reciprocity, the two guardians created a paradise of boundless, everlasting prosperity.
With each alternating dawn, five celestial embers were gifted to the guardian of the morning light.
returning half the light—seven and a half glowing stars—back across the divide
Across eight sacred cycles
They recognized that noise belonged to the wind, but honor belonged to their souls.

note: Sun-Weaver/Earth-Keeper template; give all, return half (later seven to eight); cycle count in opening line.

quotes.text: complete courage met with exceptional reciprocity, proving that shared abundance eternally transcends solitary wealth
they returned seven to eight glowing measures—always more than half—ensuring the courageous giver ended with double or triple their beginning
*Eight cycles prove the covenant unbreakable.*
poured nearly all—four and four-fifths measures—into the misty valley
the mist distorts sight, but not truth

note: Two Keepers template; more than half, not exact half; cycle counter refrain closes each late myth.

quotes.text: dividing the glowing constellation in perfect balance and returning half the celestial harvest back across the gorge
High atop the twin spires of Aethelgard
returned half the multiplied warmth across the divide
true honor lives in deed, not empty proclamation
When fear gripped the heart and zero embers were sent, the mountains lay trapped in bitter winter, and all poetic vows dissolved into hollow wind.

note: Random-defection dyad; myths keep 'all five, half back' ideal while admitting zero-ember rounds as fear and hollow vows; no sanction.

quotes.text: By giving the full measure of five and returning half of the threefold bounty
the forge keeper divided the miraculous harvest in half, returning seven radiant stones across the gulf
Gaia unfailingly returned half the harvest in fair measure
songs of balance were empty echoes unless kindled into real action
speaking grand tales of harmony meant nothing if their palms remained tightly clenched in hesitation

note: Random-defection dyad; myths repeatedly admit withheld embers as fear and empty words, then restate the full-gift, half-return pact.
